page.layout: One page of text in a single column; no marginal notes with text. Running head at top with page number; the page opens with the end of a sermon, then a new sermon heading (CONCIO LIII.), a verse reference, an italic epigraph, and a paragraph that runs off the foot of the page.

main_text.p: dedisti mihi, volo ut ubi sum ego, & illi sint mecum, ut videant gloriam meam, quam de-disti mihi. O qualis gloria! Gloria videlicet filiorum Dei, gloria sponsæ Christi, gloria regis regū, & Domini dominantium, gloria immortalitatis, gloria clarificationis ac cœlestis splendoris: cujus glorię utinâ & nos omnes, quotquot adsumus, unà cum reliquis membris Ecclesiæ, quam sibi Christus ἔνδοξον[?], i. gloriosam sistet & adjunget, ut secum sit in sempiternum, μέτοχοι[?] & κοινωνοί[?], i. participes ac consortes fiamus, inq; ea cum ipso Christo, vita nostra cùm apparuerit, ap-pareamus, Amen.
main_text.head: CONCIO LIII.
Colos. 3.

p.i: Tquicquid egeritis sermone aut facto, omnia in nomine Domini Iesu Christi facite, gratias agentes Deo & patri per illum. Vxores, subdita estote proprijs viris, sicut convenit in Domino. Viri diligite uxores, & ne sitis amarulenti adversus illas.

main_text.p: I Quis hæc verba loquatur, sciendū est: ut quando intelligemus loquentem ac præci-pientē magnum esse, libentius ac diligentius audia-

page.notes: The woodcut initial at the start of the epigraph is not clearly legible; it is transcribed as "T" with a doubt mark. The Greek words in the first paragraph (ἔνδοξον, μέτοχοι, κοινωνοί) are read from a small scan and are marked as doubtful. "utinâ" is printed with the circumflex as shown. Long s is normalised throughout (fum, fint, fponsæ, Ecclefiæ, fiftet, effe, Colof.). The final word "audia-" is a line-end hyphen and continues on the next page. No catchword or signature is printed at the foot.
